profileEvidence.summary: Sprightly and perky, English White Terriers combined house-companion lives with an ability to kill rats. Their early fanciers showed them in town public houses, and later kennels in London and Lancashire helped establish their place on the show bench. The variety gained a club of its own in the 1890s.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: Perky house companions with ratting ability, English White Terriers became a distinctive part of Britain's early dog shows.
